description_full: Pitney Bowes Inc. provides digital shipping solutions, mailing innovation, and financial services worldwide. It operates through SendTech Solutions and Presort Services segments. The SendTech Solutions segment offers physical and digital shipping and mailing technology solutions and other applications for sending, tracking, and receiving of letters, parcels and flats, as well as supplies and maintenance services. This segment also provides financing alternatives to finance other manufacturers' equipment and product purchases. The Presort Services segment operates as a workshare partner of the United States Postal Service; and offers mail sortation services. It markets its products, solutions, and services through direct and inside sales force, partner channels, direct mailings, and digital channels. The company was formerly known as Pitney Bowes Postage Meter Company. Pitney Bowes Inc. was incorporated in 1920 and is headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut.

financial_summary: Pitney Bowes Inc. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $2.1B market cap on $1.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -19% over the past three years and -6% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at -0% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 51% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $317M in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.65× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.6× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
